result:
Post revisions are in: each successful edit now keeps the post's previous version, and authors can view that history and restore any version from it. `bun run typecheck` passes, `bun test` passes (9 tests, including 7 new ones), and `bunx guren gate` passes all six stages.

- **Saving and restoring:** saving the old version and writing the new one happen in a single database transaction, so a save that fails keeps nothing. A save that is refused never gets that far.
- **Restoring:** a restore goes through the same path as an edit. The version being replaced is kept as a new revision and the restored one stays in the list, which matches the worked example (the list ends up as `Third`, `Second`, `First`).
- **Access:** both new routes use the existing author-only edit permission and sit behind the sign-in check. Other signed-in users get 403 and guests are sent to `/login`. A revision that belongs to a different post gets 404, even when the same author owns both posts.
- **Deleting a post:** the delete action removes the post's revisions itself, in the same transaction as the post. The table also has an `ON DELETE CASCADE` foreign key, but SQLite only enforces foreign keys when the connection turns them on, so I didn't rely on it.
- **Page:** the revisions page is `/posts/<id>/revisions`, and the post page now shows the author a "History" link to it.

Summary: I added a `post_revisions` table (`id`, `post_id`, `title`, `excerpt`, `body`, `created_at` as ISO text) to `db/schema.ts` with a generated migration under `db/migrations/20260925035452_add_post_revisions/`. There is a new `PostRevision` model in `app/Models/PostRevision.ts`, whose `replaceContent()` keeps the current version and overwrites the post in one transaction. `PostController.update` now uses it, and `PostController.destroy` deletes the post's revisions along with the post. A new `PostRevisionController` handles `GET /posts/:id/revisions` (named `posts.revisions.index`, props `revisions: [{ id, title, createdAt, … }]`, newest first) and `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` (named `posts.revisions.restore`, redirects to `/posts/:id`). Those routes are registered in `routes/web.ts` with a new `PostRevisionParamSchema` in `PostValidator.ts`. I also added a `PostRevisionResource`, the `resources/js/pages/posts/Revisions.tsx` page, the History link in `Show.tsx`, regenerated `.guren/*.gen.ts`, and wrote `tests/PostRevisionController.test.ts` to cover the contract.
